why_here.Home valley: a sheltered basin where the Sleepwater leaves the uplands: water, a mill head, flat ground, hills on three sides
why_here.the Frostline: a glacier's cirque above the valley: the Sleepwater's source, a tarn, snow late into summer
why_here.Driftwood: the cove at the Sleepwater's mouth, sheltered by the Headland: the valley's landing place
why_here.Fernhollow: timber in the wet woods of the Fern hills, the valley's east wall
why_here.Cogsworth: coal and iron in the coal hills, the fast Cog for power (the Millrace), and the valley floor for a railway out
why_here.Lullford: the lowest place the Lull can be bridged: gravel terraces narrow the floodplain and an island takes the piers
why_here.Gullwick: a cove on the open coast west of the delta: fish, and a beach to haul boats
why_here.Neon Harbour: a deep, sheltered ria clear of the Lull's silt; the falls gave the first crossing, the head of navigation and mill power
why_here.Launch Cape: an exposed headland past the city: rockets go up over open sea, away from people
why_here.Palm Spring: the Willow Run sinks into the gravel and comes up again here: the first water in the dry country
why_here.Dust Gulch: where the Amber leaves the mountains: water, the mine above, the railhead
why_here.the Lode: iron and copper in the massif foothills, reached by a mule track
why_here.Hearthold: a rock between two lava flows below the crater: the only defensible ground on the volcano's seaward side
why_here.Ember forge: the crater's heat at the caldera lip; ore comes down from the Lode by cart
why_here.Cinder Springs: hot springs where the sea seeps into the volcano's warm flank
why_here.Cinderwick: a black-sand cove between the flows: charcoal and fish
why_here.Lagoon Landing: the main isle's lagoon: a drowned crater of the old arc, sheltered water

Lullford Bridge: old stone arches resting on a river island, with an iron swing span for the barges (W7)

Crossroads.purpose: the market and meeting point of the valley: four lanes and two roads meet here; the farms round it bring grain, wool and fruit to its market, and the halt, the mill and the smithy serve the whole valley
Crossroads.setting: the valley floor either side of the Sleepwater, on its flat terraces; the woodland and the stone circle to the north-west
neighbourhoods: the zone as built: the square, the well, the bakery, the herbalist, the smithy, the library
south along the Sleepwater: the mill, the granary, millers' and carters' cottages
south-west down the lane to the halt: cottages with long gardens, the halt and its goods shed
east where the Foothill Road and the Lull Road leave: the drovers' market, the inn, the farrier
a short row on the woodland's skirt, foresters' and hurdle-makers' cottages

outskirts.name: the halt farms
outskirts.why: grain, hay and apples for the market

outskirts.name: the mill farms
outskirts.why: wheat for the mill, orchards on the river terrace

Dust Gulch.purpose: the desert line's railhead and the Lode's ore yard: ore comes down the mule track to the depot, goods and water go out along the line; repair shops, the assay office and the corrals for the caravans; the Amber gives it water
Dust Gulch.setting: where the Amber leaves the mountains, on the gravel fan either side of the river; desert all round, the Glass field to the west
neighbourhoods: the frontier main street: the saloon, the store, the sheriff (Pendle), the assay office
the platform, the goods yard and sheds, the repair shop and the water tower
homes along the river and its gardens, behind the main street
homes and the chapel on the west bank
pens and stables for the caravans and the mule trains, east of town

outskirts.name: the corrals
outskirts.why: pens and stables for the caravans and the mule trains

outskirts.name: the goods yard
outskirts.why: the desert line's sidings and the ore bins

outskirts.name: the ore yard
outskirts.why: the Lode's ore, down the mule track, waiting for the train

Palm Spring.purpose: the first water in the dry country: the Willow Run comes up again in the spring; irrigated gardens, date and fig orchards, the caravans' rest on the Drover's Road, and the diviner (Mirra) who keeps the spring
Palm Spring.setting: round the spring pool and along its two channels, on the gravel where the Willow Run resurfaces; scrub and steppe round it
neighbourhoods: houses round the pool under the palms
the inn, stables and stores on the Drover's Road
gardeners' houses along the south-west channel
along the south-east channel to the orchards

outskirts.name: the date gardens
outskirts.why: date palms, figs and vegetables on the channels

Fernhollow.purpose: timber from the Fern hills' wet woods: the sawmill, the wood yards and the joiners; charcoal for Cogsworth; its own green, school and chapel, on the Foothill Road halfway between Crossroads and Cogsworth
Fernhollow.setting: a clearing in the woods of the Fern hills, where the Foothill Road crosses Fern Lane
neighbourhoods: houses round the village green, the chapel and the school
the sawmill and the wood yards, joiners and coopers
cottages down the lane to the Lull Road

outskirts.name: the wood yards
outskirts.why: the Fern hills' timber, seasoning in stacks

Cogsworth.purpose: coal and iron from the coal hills, the fast Cog for power (the Millrace), and the railway out: the foundry, the mills, the engine works and the terminus; brick terraces for the workers between the works and the pits
Cogsworth.setting: the Cog's east bank where the valley opens, between the river and the coal hills; the pits and spoil heaps above it
neighbourhoods: the foundry, the mills on the Millrace, workshops by the river
shops and the works offices on the towpath road down to the terminus
brick workers' terraces climbing toward the pits
the platform, the station square and the Garth Road's start

outskirts.name: the railway yard
outskirts.why: the terminus sidings, the engine shed and the coal stage

outskirts.name: the allotments
outskirts.why: the terraces' vegetable plots

Hearthold.purpose: the fire country's town of knights and crafts: the castle on its rock commands the only stable ground between the lava flows; armourers, smiths, potters and vintners under the walls; the lower town on the flat ground below, toward the springs and the coast
Hearthold.setting: a rock between two lava flows below the crater, ringed by its town wall; the old flow's weathered ash below it farmed
neighbourhoods: inside the wall: the keep, the hall, the barracks and drill yard, the chapel, the knights' houses
forges and armourers against the cooled lava, east of the gate market
the gate market, the inn and the shops below the gate
potters', vintners' and smiths' terraces stepping down the slope

outskirts.name: the drill yard
outskirts.why: the knights' and the guard's training ground, beside the barracks

outskirts.name: the castle yard
outskirts.why: basalt setts inside the wall

outskirts.name: the vines
outskirts.why: vines on the cooled ash of the rock's warm east side

Cinderwick.purpose: the fire country's harbour: fishing boats and the coaster that calls for Hearthold's goods; charcoal kilns and a black-sand glassworks; the quay is the region's way to the sea
Cinderwick.setting: a black-sand cove between the flows, the young flow steaming to the east; the Ash Coast path and the Ember Way meet here
neighbourhoods: fishers' houses and net lofts along the beach
the kilns, the glassworks and the coopers
the stone quay, the chandler and the harbour office

outskirts.name: the kilns
outskirts.why: charcoal from the dead forest; black-sand glass

Lagoon Landing.purpose: the isles' town: boats, fishing and the diving trade off the reef wrecks (Brine), the naturalist's house, net and sail lofts, the boatyard; the ferry to Driftwood and the boats to the other isles leave from here
Lagoon Landing.setting: the neck of the main isle between the ferry pier on the open north shore and the sheltered lagoon (a drowned crater)
neighbourhoods: boathouses and stilt houses on the lagoon
net and sail lofts, the chandler
the ferry pier, the harbour office and the inn

outskirts.name: the boatyard

Highgarth.purpose: an old post town on the pass road: lodgings, stores and the lord's watch on the north pass; slate from its quarry, wool from the summer pastures and timber from the valley's larches go down to Cogsworth. Its trade over the pass stopped when the Starfall brought the rockfall down, and the lord sealed the pass: the road beyond waits for a later region
Highgarth.setting: a sheltered valley on the upper Cog inside the range: Garth Street along the valley floor, the temple on its plinth up the east slope, terraces stepping down to the river, snow on the peaks round it
neighbourhoods: the post road: machiya wall to wall, the two post inns, the post square
the main hall, the pagoda and the gravel court on their plinth; the pine grove and the shrine path
thatched farmhouses and storehouses up the east slope; the slate quarry
the sawmill by the Cog, the bathhouse and the moon-viewing terrace
